findings.evidence: "Open the alerts panel from the console sidebar and select the rule you want to adjust."
findings.fix: Split into two separate steps: one for opening the alerts panel, and a second for selecting the rule to adjust.
findings.location: Open alert settings section, first sentence
findings.violation: The step combines two distinct actions, opening the panel and selecting a rule, into a single sentence, which makes it harder to follow and to verify that each action was completed.

findings.fix: Name the specific console or product on first use, or add a lead-in sentence before the first heading stating what is being configured and in which product.
findings.location: Open alert settings section, first sentence
findings.violation: "The console" is used without ever being introduced or named, so a reader arriving at this document without other context cannot be sure which product or console is meant.

findings.evidence: "A threshold is the numeric boundary that triggers an alert once a metric crosses it."
findings.fix: Move this definition to an introductory or concepts section before the numbered steps, or remove it if the term is already defined elsewhere.
findings.location: Open alert settings section, second sentence
findings.violation: This is a conceptual definition rather than an instructional step, and its placement inside a how-to procedure interrupts the sequence of actions the document's own frontmatter promises.

findings.evidence: "confirm the unit matches the metric in use"
findings.fix: Add a sentence explaining how to change the unit, or where to find the correct unit, when it does not match.
findings.location: Set the new threshold section, first sentence
findings.violation: The instruction does not say what to do if the unit does not match, leaving the reader with no next action in that case.

findings.evidence: "This is because the console applies the new threshold to every future evaluation of this rule."
findings.fix: Remove the explanation from the step sequence, or move it into a clearly separated note so the actionable steps read continuously.
findings.location: Set the new threshold section, second sentence
findings.violation: This is an explanatory aside placed between instructional steps, interrupting the procedure with rationale instead of the next action to take.

findings.evidence: "Save the rule and open the rule list to confirm the new threshold appears there."
findings.fix: Split into a save step and a separate verification step, and add what to do if verification fails, such as retrying or checking for an error message.
findings.violation: This step combines saving and verifying into a single sentence and gives no guidance for what to do if the new threshold does not appear in the list.

findings.fix: Retitle to reflect the single-rule scope, for example "Configure an alert threshold," or expand the body to cover multiple rules.
findings.violation: The plural title suggests configuring thresholds across multiple alerts or rules, but the body only ever walks through adjusting a single rule's threshold.

findings.evidence: the document goes directly from the title "# Configure alert thresholds" to the first heading "## Open alert settings" with no lead-in text
findings.fix: Add one or two introductory sentences after the title stating what the procedure accomplishes and any prerequisites needed before starting.
findings.location: beginning of the document, immediately after the title
findings.violation: There is no introductory sentence stating the goal, outcome, or prerequisites of the procedure before the steps begin, so a reader starts step one without knowing what they will accomplish.
